specs.note: standard install · see the drawer for the reference point

rows: hot at all times, no switch

steps: Pick the design option

Standard, Komfort Zone Kit (KZK-036 or KZK-1510A) or Kozy Power Vent (KPV, horizontal only): framing, clearances, venting and the approved safety barriers all follow from it. Chamber and ceiling minimum: 72" standard, 82" with a KZK.

Decide before setting the unit, and read every section that applies to your option.

  • Standard: chamber and ceiling minimum 72" (1829mm); only the safety barriers in Figure 2.2.
  • Komfort Zone Kit: redistributes radiant heat through plenums, allowing combustible facing above, heat reduction for a TV above and lower mantel clearances. Chamber minimum 82" (2083mm); framing per the kit manual. Before setting the unit (and before the stand-offs), remove the top outer shell assembly (11 screws), discard the 4 cover plates, the insulation and the bottom section of the top assembly, then refit the top piece with the 11 screws.
  • Kozy Power Vent #KPV: fan-powered, horizontal terminations only; it doesn't change facing, finishing or safety barrier requirements.

Barriers B36-PSF2 and B36-FRSF2 are approved only with KZK-036 or KZK-1510A, and the rope on their back must be removed and discarded. The unit may go in a bedroom, and in an aftermarket, permanently located manufactured home (USA only) or mobile home where local codes allow. Outdoor covered installs: operation approved from 40°F to 110°F; black painted barriers recommended.
Frame the opening

Frame to Figure 3.4 (the rough-in is the same for every design option; KZK framing per its manual) on a level surface that carries the fireplace and venting. Lay out the vent path first and frame the wall pass-through to Figure 3.6.

• Set the fireplace directly on wood or a non-combustible surface, not linoleum or carpet. On carpeting, tile or other combustible material other than wood flooring, use a metal or wood panel the full width and depth of the unit. Above floor level, build a solid, continuous platform.
  • No floor protection is required in front. The bottom of the fireplace must be level with the finished hearth for the safety barrier to fit.
  • Allow for wall covering and facing thickness. Insulate outside walls (cold air transfer area). Masonry above needs a foundation for the full load and a lintel over the appliance.
  • Leave room in front for barrier removal, component access, the gas line and service.
  • If possible, place the unit so the vent terminates between two studs. Horizontal runs need 1/4" rise per 12" and wall thimbles that meet the 1" top clearance; elbow heights vary by vent maker (Figure 3.6 uses a Simpson DuraVent elbow).

Figures 3.4 and 3.6 give the framing dimensions as drawings only.
Fit the finishing trim kit

B36-FTK comes with the fireplace and is highly recommended: it ensures the safety barrier fits and gives finishing material an edge to stop against. Attach it before installing the fireplace; the top trim panel goes on before the top stand-offs and nailing flanges.

1. Remove and save the screws holding the side heat shields and the nailing flanges.
  2. Fit the side trim pieces to the holes in the sides of the unit; the heat shields and nailing flanges go back on top of them with the saved screws.
  3. Remove the top stand-off screws, align the top trim panel with the front stand-off holes and secure it; the top stand-off assembly is built on top of it (next step).
  4. Remove and discard the existing bottom front frame portion if fitted, and slot the new bottom trim piece into the bottom corners of the unit.
Stand-offs, flanges & set the unit

Form and fit the top stand-offs (they provide the 8" minimum to the header; non-combustible material only in that zone) and the nailing flanges (7/16" from the sides to framing). Set the fireplace in the opening and fasten it through the flanges, flush with the framing.

1. Top stand-offs: remove the 2 screws holding the stand-off heat shields and brackets, bend each bracket at its perforations, align it with the holes in the fireplace top and secure with those 2 screws plus the 2 on top.
  2. Form the stand-off heat shields (flange up and to the back) and fix them to the brackets with the 8 screws from the fireplace components packet.
  3. Nailing flanges: remove them from the sides, align with the holes on the outside corners (stand-off flanges facing away), screw through the slots, and bend the perforation parallel with the fireplace face, never toward it.
  4. Set the fireplace with the framing studs against the small stand-offs on the back of the flanges; nail or screw. With the trim kit fitted, the trim sticks out past the framing.
Never permanently remove the nailing flanges, whatever the finish. Use no wood or sheetrock in the stand-off zone, for the full width of the fireplace. With a KZK, finish the kit prep before building the stand-offs.
Vent connection

Fit the supplied vent heat shield (required in every venting scenario) and, if used, the restrictor plate before the vent goes on. Run approved 4" × 6-5/8" co-axial pipe with 1" clearance (17-5/8" above horizontal pipe inside the chamber) and 1/4" rise per 12".

• Provide a way to visually check the vent connection after the fireplace is installed.
  • Restrictor plate (components packet): shipped with both inner rings intact for the most restriction; knock out one or both for less. It can also go in later through the fireplace baffle (step 10).
  • Attic insulation shields and wall thimbles may be insulated with unfaced insulation listed non-combustible per ASTM E 136.
  • Flexible vent pipe only outside the appliance enclosure, and never to terminate the system. Never connect to a chimney flue serving a solid-fuel appliance.
  • Terminate per section 7 and the vent maker's instructions; don't recess a horizontal cap into the wall or siding.

Run lengths, elbows and chimney conversions: see the Venting card.
Gas line + leak test

Connect a listed 1/2" tee-handle shut-off and flexible connector to the 1/2" control valve inlet (a 3/8" × 18" flexible connector and shut-off come with the fireplace), routed through the gas line hole without obstructing the fan. Check every connection, field or factory, with soapy water.

• Qualified person only, to local codes or ANSI Z223.1; in Massachusetts, a licensed plumber or gas fitter and a Massachusetts-approved shut-off valve.
  • Supply-line pressure tests: disconnect the appliance and its shut-off above 1/2 psi (3.5 kPa); at or below that, isolate it by closing its manual shut-off.
  • Built for natural gas. For propane, use the certified kit (LCK-NK36-S; the stepper motor is sold separately) and convert before fitting light kit components or the log set.
  • High altitude: get the rating method from the local gas distributor or the authority having jurisdiction.

Gas line access is shown on the dimension drawing (Figure 2.1, p. 9), as a drawing only.
Electrical

Feed the junction box 120VAC, 60Hz, 6 Amps from a supply that is hot at all times with no switch, grounded to local code, the National Electrical Code (ANSI/NFPA 70) or CSA C22.1. Plug the three-prong cord into a grounded receptacle.

• Shut off the household breaker before working on any electrical line.
  • Don't cut or remove the grounding prong.
  • Battery backup runs the burner and flame modulation; the fan and lights need the 120 VAC supply.
  • Harnesses: 120v main 700-350, fan/light kit 700-655, ember bed AUX 800-AUX, ON/OFF 700-656, IFC 700-653; spade connectors are marked M (male) and F (female).
  • Outdoor covered installs: all wiring to the outdoor requirements of NFPA 70.

The wiring diagram (Figures 10.1–10.3, pp. 49–51) is a drawing only.
Facing & finishing

Finish last, after the vent, gas and wiring. Hold every clearance, use true non-combustible material where required (drywall, Type X and WonderBoard don't qualify), and keep finishing clear of the ventilation air and the safety barrier.

• A 37-3/4" × 10-1/2" non-combustible board is supplied; it covers more than the minimum non-combustible zone (Figure 5.5, p. 29, a drawing).
  • Mantel, hearth and sidewall rules: see the Mantel & facing card. KZK installs follow the kit manual.
  • To help avoid sheetrock cracking above the unit: dry, dust-free surfaces; heat-resilient tape, mesh and joint compound (such as Durabond), cured per the maker; high-quality acrylic latex primer and finish coat; avoid flat or light-colored paints.
  • Marble, granite or stone: never a one-piece U-shaped surround (thermal expansion can crack it); the material must handle temperatures greater than 160°F.

Kozy Heat disclaims damage to finishing materials (warping, discoloring, cracking, peeling, flaking) and off-gassing or smells from them when heated.
Lights, media & logs

Convert to propane first if needed, and disconnect power. Fit the halogen bulbs with a soft cloth (the front bottom light kit's 5 come in the components packet), set the media tray side trim for your panel choice, then install any panel set and the log set (NK36-500 or NK36-B501) per its own instructions.

• Front bottom light kit: no bulbs from the factory. Remove the barrier, glass, logs and media, lift out the log rack/ember media tray (4 screws) and fit the 5 halogen bulbs.
  • Back bottom and top light kits come with bulbs fitted; replacing the back bottom bulbs means removing the left and right burners (7/16" nuts) and the back media tray.
  • No panel set, or NK36-BG900: make sure the logs and ember bed media butt up against the firebox so no light shines through from the bottom light kit.
  • NK36-HB900, NK36-L900, NK36-BB900 or NK36-CB900: remove and discard the 2 side trim pieces and their 4 screws so the side refractory lies flat.
  • Glass: hook its slots over the top tabs, lower the bottom and pull the 2 spring latches out and up. Then hang the safety barrier (section 5.3); on louvered barriers, match the louver notch to the notched-tab position.
Initialize, test & tune

Clear packaging from the firebox, fit 4 AA backup and 3 AAA remote batteries, power the IFC module and pair the remote. Check inlet and manifold pressures, let it burn 15 minutes, then adjust venturis or the restrictor only if the flame calls for it.

1. Rocker switch OFF; batteries in; IFC module on AC power.
  2. Remove the safety barrier and bottom frame, slide out the control module and press the remote sync button: 3 beeps and an amber LED.
  3. Within 5 seconds press ON/OFF on the remote: 4 beeps and the pilot lights. Press ON/OFF again; the pilot goes out and the system is initialized.
  4. Rocker switch ON for remote operation; refit the bottom frame and the safety barrier.

Pressures: see the Inlet and Manifold cards. Venturi factory settings: NG left/right 1/8", LP left/right 5/16", rear 3/8" (fully open). Venturi adjustment is for a qualified service technician, in slight increments, with the unit cool.

Dark orange flame, black tipsventuri closed too far: open slightly
Short, blue flamesventuri open too far: close slightly
Lifting (ghosting) flamesgas pressure too high and/or venturi closed too far: check manometer, open slightly
Short, flickering flameexcessive draft: add restrictor plate
Lifting or ghosting (draft)insufficient draft: remove inner ring(s) or the restrictor plate
Note: Table 12.4 (p. 61) says lifting (ghosting) flames mean gas pressure too high and/or the venturi closed too far, so open the venturi slightly; section 12.2.1 (p. 61) says opening the air shutter causes a short, blue flame that may lift off the burner, and the troubleshooting chart (p. 65) says to close the shutter slightly for a flame that burns blue and lifts off the burner.

Restrictor access is through the fireplace baffle (4 screws): bend the tabs to about 80° and insert it into the 4" exhaust with the tabs toward you. If flames still lift or ghost after opening the restrictor and verifying the vent, shut off the gas supply and call a qualified service technician.

panels.title: Pilot won't light, stay lit or go out
items: Power interrupted or disconnected → restore power, or run on battery back-up with fully charged batteries
Wiring disconnection → check every connection against the wiring schematic
Gas supply off → check the shut-off valves; there may be more than one between appliance and main line
No propane, or low gas pressure (bent line, too-narrow pipe, low line pressure) → refill; consult a plumber or gas supplier
Pilot adjustment screw not sealed → seal it; don't over-tighten
Pilot not contacting the flame rectification sensor → it must envelop the top of the sensor and reach far enough onto the burner
Pilot always on, won't go out → system set to CPI; set it to IPI

panels.title: Burner won't light, or no reaction to commands
items: ON/OFF rocker switch OFF → switch it ON
Gas off or low supply → check for multiple shut-offs, the propane tank; consult a plumber or gas supplier
Wiring disconnected or wrong → check against Figure 10.1
Plugged burner orifice → remove the blockage
Pilot flame not directed to ignite the burner → correct it
No call for heat → remote powered ON and thermostat operation turned OFF
Remote or backup batteries low → replace them
No communication between remote and control module → reprogram the remote to the IFC module
Maximum failed ignitions or flame restorations reached → reset the IFC module

panels.title: Pilot & burner go out while running
items: No propane in tank → refill
Glass assembly installed incorrectly → refit per section 9.1
Vent cap installed incorrectly or blocked → adjust; remove debris
Horizontal venting without 1/4" rise per 12" of travel → correct the pitch
Exhaust pipe leaking exhaust back into the firebox → find and repair leaks
Excessive draft → install or modify a restrictor (section 12.2.3)

panels.title: Soot on glass, or blue flame lifting off
items: Soot: improper log placement → reset the logs per section 9.5
Soot: venturi settings → open the air shutters slightly for more air
Blue flame lifting off the burner: venturi setting → close the shutter slightly for less air (Table 12.4 says to open the venturi slightly for lifting or ghosting flames)
Either: vent cap installed incorrectly or blocked → adjust; remove debris
Lifting flame: vent pipes leaking → check for leaks and repair

codes: Backup pack below 4V: low double-beep on ON/OFF and no commands accepted until the batteries are replaced.
No flame after 2 ignition tries. Verify gas is on and the sensor isn't shorted; reset, or re-initialize (section 11.2).

light.title: Turning the fireplace on and off
light.html:
Your fireplace lights itself: the control module sparks the pilot, and the pilot lights the burner. You run it from the remote.

Turn it on

  1. Make sure the main ON/OFF rocker switch is ON. It's on the left side of the unit, behind the safety screen (lift the screen up and out of its slots).
  2. Press ON/OFF on the remote. The fireplace beeps once to confirm.
  3. About 4 seconds later it starts sparking at the pilot. Once the pilot is lit, the burner comes on.
  4. Set the flame with the up and down arrows.

If it doesn't light

It tries twice: about 60 seconds of sparking, a pause of about 35 seconds, then another 60 seconds. If there's still no flame, it locks out and the red light blinks 3 times, over and over. Check that the gas is on, then press ON/OFF, wait about 2 seconds and press it again (or flip the rocker switch off and back on). Repeated lockouts are a job for a qualified technician.

Red light: 1 blinkbackup batteries low
2 blinkspilot flame error: contact your dealer
3 blinkslockout

Turn it off

Press ON/OFF on the remote. The screen shows only the room temperature and the burner goes out. You can also step the flame down with the down arrow until the screen shows OFF; pressing up relights it on HI. In CPI mode the pilot stays lit after the burner goes off.

remote.title: Using the remote
remote.html:
The remote runs on 3 AAA batteries (included) and controls everything once it's paired with the fireplace.

  • ON/OFF turns the fireplace on and off.
  • Up / down arrows step through 6 flame levels. Up, while the fireplace is on but the flame is off, relights it on HI.
  • Thermostat key starts room thermostat mode: the screen shows a temperature bulb, the room temperature and your set temperature; the arrows change the setting. Press it until SMART appears for the smart thermostat, which turns the flame down as the room reaches the set point. While smart mode is on, you can't adjust the flame by hand.
  • Mode key steps to the fan, light and ember-bed (AUX) controls.
  • Key lock: press mode and up together to lock or unlock the keys against unsupervised use. A lock icon shows.
  • °F / °C: with the fireplace off, press thermostat and mode together.

If it stops responding

Replace the remote or backup batteries if they're low. If the remote and fireplace have lost touch, the remote needs re-pairing at the sync button on the control module. If too many ignitions have failed, the control module needs a reset.

No remote? The system can be reset for manual operation, where the rocker switch turns the burner on (high flame only) and off. The steps are in section 11.3.

normal.title: Flames and noises: what's normal
normal.html:
Blue at first, then yellow

When the fireplace is first lit, the flames look blue. Over the first 15 minutes they gradually turn the yellow color you want.

Reading the flame

Lazy, yellow flamesnormal, no adjustment needed
Dark, orange flamesventuri adjustment needed
Short, blue flamesventuri adjustment needed
Lifting (ghosting) flamesadjustment needed: venturi, gas pressure and/or vent system

Flames should be steady, not lifting or floating. Their height and look also vary with how the fireplace is vented and which gas it burns. Venturi (air shutter) adjustment must be done by a qualified service technician.

Noises

Some discoloration, and minor expansion, contraction or movement of parts that makes noise, is normal and not a defect.

Worth a service call: dark orange flames with black tips, or soot on the glass. Causes range from log placement to the venturi settings and the vent cap.

glass.title: Cleaning the glass
glass.html:
The manual lists glass cleaning as a once-a-year homeowner job. Do it only when the fireplace is completely cool: never clean the glass, or take it off, while it's hot.

  1. Clear a flat, stable work surface big enough to hold the glass assembly.
  2. Lift the safety screen up and out of its slots.
  3. Find the 2 spring-loaded latches at the bottom of the firebox. Pull them out and down to free the bottom of the glass, then lift the glass assembly up and off the 2 tabs at the top.
  4. Clean the glass with a fireplace glass cleaner and a soft cloth. Don't use abrasive cleaners, and take care not to scratch it.
  5. To refit, tilt the top in and hook its slots over the top tabs while you lower the bottom into place. Pull the latches out and up to lock it.
  6. Put the safety screen back. Don't run the fireplace without it.
Cracked or broken? Don't run the fireplace with the glass removed, cracked or broken, and don't strike or slam it. Wear protective gloves to handle broken glass. Replacement glass comes only from Hussong Mfg. as a complete assembly (part 701-005T) and should be fitted by a qualified service person.

modes.title: Pilot modes: IPI and CPI
modes.html:
The pilot can work two ways, and you choose with the remote.

IPIspark-to-pilot: the pilot is sparked alight each time you turn the fireplace on
CPIcontinuous (standing) pilot that stays lit while the burner is off

A standing pilot keeps the firebox warm and sets up a draft in the vent, so the main burner lights with less disruption to the air flow.

Switch modes

  1. With the fireplace off, press the mode key to step to the CPI mode icon (the snowflake shows during this setup).
  2. Press the up arrow for CPI, or the down arrow to go back to IPI. One beep confirms.

With the fireplace on, a snowflake on the screen means CPI; no snowflake means IPI.

Built-in safety timers

  • In CPI, if the main burner hasn't lit for 7 days in a row, the pilot turns off. Lighting the burner at any point resets the 7-day timer.
  • Within 24 hours of continuous pilot operation, the system turns off for about 5 seconds to check its safety functions, then goes back to your last command.

Pilot that won't go out? It's set to CPI; switch to IPI.

fan.title: Fan and lights
fan.html:
Press the mode key to step to the fan, top light or ember-bed (AUX) icon, then use the up and down arrows.

Fan6 speeds, plus on and off
Top accent light6 brightness levels
Ember-bed light (AUX)up arrow on, down arrow off

Why the fan waits

In thermostat mode, the fan holds off for 5 minutes after the fireplace lights, so heat can build, and keeps running about 12 minutes after the fireplace turns off. In manual mode it runs at its last setting with no delay.

Ember-bed brightness

The ember-bed light has its own dimmer knob under the firebox. Lift off the safety screen, turn the knob clockwise for brighter or counterclockwise for dimmer, then put the screen back.

Power outage: the fan and lights don't run on the backup batteries. The burner still does.

The remote can switch the fan, light and ember-bed (AUX) features on (SEL) or off (CLR) in a setup sequence that starts with taking one battery out (sections 11.9.8.1 to 11.9.10.2).

The bulbs are halogen and should never be touched with bare hands (use a soft cloth). Changing one means disconnecting power and taking out the glass, logs and media.

power.title: Power outages and batteries
power.html:
The fireplace runs on 120 VAC household power and has a backup battery pack, so it still works in an outage.

Backup pack (control module)4 × AA (not included)
Remote3 × AAA (included)

During an outage

The burner and flame-height adjustment keep working on the backup batteries. The fan and accent lights don't.

Low-battery signs

  • Backup pack: the fireplace double-beeps when you press ON/OFF and won't take more commands until you replace the batteries. The red light also blinks once at intervals. With fresh batteries it beeps once as soon as it's powered.
  • Remote: a battery icon appears on the screen before the batteries run out, and goes away once you replace them.

Battery life depends on battery quality and how often the fireplace lights, among other things. The backup holder is on the control module: lift off the safety screen, pull the bottom frame piece up and out, and slide the control module out. Put the bottom frame back afterward.

If any part of the fireplace has been under water, don't use it. Immediately call a qualified service technician to inspect it and to replace any part of the control system and any gas control that has been under water.

safety.title: Safety and gas smell
safety.html:
If you smell gas

  • Don't try to light any appliance.
  • Don't touch any electrical switch, and don't use any phone in your building.
  • Leave the building right away.
  • Immediately call your gas supplier from a neighbor's phone and follow their instructions. If you can't reach them, call the fire department.

Every day

  • The viewing glass gets hot. The safety screen that comes with the fireplace reduces the risk of burns and must be in place to protect children and other at-risk people. If it's damaged, replace it with Hussong Mfg.'s screen for this fireplace.
  • Never run the fireplace with the glass removed, cracked or broken, or with the safety screen off.
  • Keep it out of traffic and away from furniture and draperies. Don't store or use gasoline or other flammable vapors and liquids nearby.
  • Use the remote's key lock (mode and up together) to prevent unsupervised use.
  • If any part has been under water, don't use the fireplace. Immediately call a qualified service technician to inspect it and to replace any part of the control system and any gas control that has been under water.

Installation and service must be done by a qualified installer, service agency or the gas supplier.

service.title: Yearly service
service.html:
Have a professional service person inspect the fireplace before use and at least once a year. It may need cleaning more often if there's a lot of lint from carpeting, bedding and the like. The control compartments, burners and air passageways must be kept clean.

What the yearly service covers

  • Firebox: vacuum out debris; check the bottom glass latches move freely with spring tension.
  • Fan: disconnected and vacuumed. The bearings are sealed and need no oil.
  • Vent: the vent and outside cap checked for soot or blockage; air flow must not be obstructed.
  • Glass: cleaned and checked for cracks, scratches and nicks.
  • Burner and pilot: vacuumed and leak-checked; the pilot and flame safety system checked; the burner must light within 4 seconds of the gas valve opening, with steady flames. If the flame fails, the safety shutoff must act in no more than 30 seconds.
Your part: clean the glass once a year, and keep the area around the fireplace clear of combustible materials, gasoline and other flammable vapors and liquids.

warranty.title: Warranty at a glance
warranty.html:
Hussong Mfg. gives a Limited Lifetime Warranty to the original purchaser, from the date of purchase. It can't be transferred.

30 days · parts & laborpaint, light bulbs, gasket material, glass media and media dam
Year 1 · parts & laborall other parts and material
Years 2 to lifetime · parts onlyfirebox, heat exchanger, logs, burner tube or pan, outer shell, heat shields, front viewing glass (thermal shock only), refractory liner (not enamel or glass panels)

Labor is reimbursed to an authorized dealer only. You don't need to register; keep your proof of purchase with the date, serial number and model. If you notice a defect, contact your authorized dealer within 30 days.

Voided or not covered

  • Not installed by a licensed, authorized technician or contractor, or not installed, run and maintained per the manual
  • Serial number or testing label removed, or the fireplace altered or tampered with
  • Submersion in water, long dampness or condensation, or water damage from improper venting
  • Normal wear and tear, venting or site problems, chimney parts and non-Hussong accessories, or how well it heats your space
This is a summary. The full terms and exclusions are in the official PDF.

specInlet.title: Inlet (supply) pressure
specInlet.html:
NG min / max5" / 10" WC (1.25 / 2.49 kPa)
NG recommended7" WC (1.74 kPa)
LP min12" WC (2.99 kPa) · Table 12.1: 11" WC (2.74 kPa)
LP max13" WC (3.24 kPa)
Note: the manual gives a propane minimum inlet pressure of 12" WC (2.99 kPa) in the heating specifications (p. 8) and Table 6.1 (p. 33), and 11" WC (2.74 kPa) in Table 12.1 (p. 60).

Test at the valve's IN tap with all other gas appliances in the house on, or at full capacity: loosen the screw counter-clockwise, attach a manometer with a 1/4" I.D. hose, light pilot and burner and read. Turn them off, remove the hose and snug the screw (don't over-tighten), then relight and re-check that the tap reads no pressure. Too high or too low: contact the gas company; only a qualified gas service technician adjusts incoming pressure.

Supply-line tests: disconnect the appliance and its shut-off above 1/2 psi (3.5 kPa); at or below that, close its manual shut-off.

specManifold.title: Manifold pressure
specManifold.html:
NG low – high1.1" – 3.8" WC (0.27 – 0.95 kPa)
LP low – high2.9" – 11" WC (0.72 – 2.74 kPa)

The valve's OUT tap reads manifold (outgoing) pressure. Light the pilot, loosen the OUT screw counter-clockwise, attach the manometer (1/4" I.D. hose), light the burner and compare with Table 12.2. Turn burner and pilot off, remove the hose and snug the screw (don't over-tighten), then reattach the manometer to confirm the tap is sealed: it should read no pressure with pilot and burner on.

Flame appearance tables (venturi and restrictor): step 10.

specVent.title: Venting
specVent.html:
Co-axial 4" (102mm) exhaust × 6-5/8" (168mm) intake, natural draft, from an approved maker: American Metal Products (Ameri-Vent), BDM, ICC, Metal Fab, Olympia Chimney Supply, Selkirk or Simpson DuraVent (cap part numbers in Table 8.1). Kozy Heat Power Vent #KPV (sold separately) follows its own manual.

Vertical3' min · 50' max + cap
12" vertical + 90°48" max horizontal
24" vertical + 90°10' max horizontal
36" vertical + 90°14' max horizontal
25' max vertical + 90°25' max horizontal
Combination25' rise + 25' run = 50' total; max (5) 90° elbows
Extra elbowssubtract 3' per 90° after the first; (2) 45° may replace (1) 90°, subtract 18" per 45°

Combination terminations must fall in the shaded area of Figure 8.6 (p. 41), shown only as a chart. The supplied vent heat shield is required in all venting scenarios. Flexible pipe only outside the appliance enclosure, never to terminate. Never share a flue with a solid-fuel appliance.

Chimney conversions

Class A / masonry (existing min 7" ID)90° elbow + retro connector + 4" aluminum flex, 10' min / 50' max + top adapter + cap
Co-axial to co-linear90° elbow + co-linear adapter + 3" × 3" aluminum flex, 10' min / 40' max + cap

Both allow 0" to 24" of horizontal run (rigid or flexible). Have the chimney inspected first and confirm the local building jurisdiction allows it.

specTerm.html:
Natural-draft terminations. Clearances are to heat-resistant material such as wood or metal, not vinyl: Hussong Mfg. isn't responsible for heat damage under vinyl soffits, ceilings or overhangs.

* In accordance with local installation codes and the gas supplier's requirements. Canada: no termination directly above a sidewalk or paved driveway between two single-family dwellings that serves both. Don't recess the cap into the wall or siding. Vertical cap clearances are drawn in Figures 7.1–7.2 (p. 34), as diagrams only.

Massachusetts: where a sidewall termination is less than 7 feet above finished grade, CO detectors are required (hard-wired with alarm and battery back-up on the appliance's floor level) and a "GAS VENT DIRECTLY BELOW. KEEP CLEAR OF ALL OBSTRUCTIONS" plate at least 8 feet above grade in line with the terminal (section 1.3, p. 7).

Table 3.1, standard installation, based on nominal 2" × 4" framing. The top stand-offs provide the 8" (203mm) minimum to the header: only non-combustible material in that zone, for the full width (no wood or sheetrock). Nailing flanges give 7/16" (11mm) from the fireplace sides to framing. After the wall pass-through, horizontal pipe needs 1" (25mm) on all surfaces.

With a Komfort Zone Kit (KZK-036 or KZK-1510A) the chamber minimum becomes 82" (2083mm) and clearances may change: use the kit's manual. Mantel and sidewall rules: Mantel & facing card. Framing (Figure 3.4, p. 17) and appliance dimensions (Figure 2.1, p. 9) are shown only as drawings.

specMantel.title: Mantel, hearth & facing
specMantel.html:
Standard installation, with screen barriers NK36-PSVF, NK36-RSVF, B36A-MSF2 or B36R-MSF2. With B36-PSF2 or B36-FRSF2 (Komfort Zone Kit installs only), take hearth, mantel and sidewall projections from the KZK manual.

3/4" combustible mantel trim8" (203mm) above the top
6" (152mm) combustible mantel11-1/2" (292mm) above the top
Deeper mantels+1" (25mm) of depth for every 1" (25mm) of height above the 6" mantel
8" non-combustible mantelfrom 32-3/4" (832mm) above the fireplace base, flush with the B36-FTK top
8" non-combustible surroundflush at the trim kit's side and top finishing edge; 1" up for every 1" deeper
Combustible sidewallunlimited, from 3/4" (19mm) off the fireplace side (0" to the trim kit side)
Combustible hearthunlimited projection; not raised above the fireplace base / enclosure floor
Supplied non-combustible board37-3/4" × 10-1/2"
Note: Table 3.1 (p. 15) measures the 8" mantel-trim and 11-1/2" mantel clearances from the fireplace top; section 5.1.1 (p. 24) gives the same figures above the top finishing edge.

Drywall (including Type X) and WonderBoard are not non-combustible. The minimum non-combustible zone is drawn in Figure 5.5 (p. 29) and the mantel projections in Figures 5.2–5.3 (pp. 26–27). Finishing must not block ventilation air or safety barrier removal.

TV above the fireplace: the KZK design option is highly recommended, with the plenum discharge above the TV and a mantel to deflect heat; TV temperatures are the homeowner's responsibility.

specElec.title: Electrical
specElec.html:
Junction box120VAC, 60Hz, 6 Amps

Battery backup(4) AA in the control module: burner and flame modulation only

Shut off the household breaker before working on any electrical line. Ground per local codes, or the National Electrical Code ANSI/NFPA 70 or Canadian Electrical Code CSA C22.1; never cut or remove the grounding prong. Fan and light components don't run on battery backup.

Harnesses: 120v main 700-350 · fan/light kit 700-655 · ember bed AUX 800-AUX · ON/OFF 700-656 · IFC 700-653. Wiring is drawn in Figures 10.1–10.3 (pp. 49–51). Label all wires before disconnecting; wiring errors can cause improper and dangerous operation. Outdoor covered installs: wiring to the outdoor requirements of NFPA 70; operation approved from 40°F to 110°F.

conflicts.issue: Propane minimum inlet pressure: 12" WC (2.99 kPa) in 2.1 Heating Specifications and Table 6.1; 11" WC (2.74 kPa) in Table 12.1 Inlet Pressures. Maximum 13" WC agrees.

Combustible mantel reference point: Table 3.1 gives 8" to a 3/4" mantel trim and 11-1/2" to a 6" deep mantel measured from the fireplace top; 5.1.1 gives the same figures above the top finishing edge (5.1.2 places that edge on the finishing trim kit, with a 3/4" gap to the fireplace in its drawing).

Venturi direction for lifting flames: 12.2.1 says opening the air shutter gives a short, blue flame that may lift off the burner, and the troubleshooting chart says close the shutter slightly for a flame that burns blue and lifts; Table 12.4 says lifting (ghosting) flames mean gas pressure too high and/or venturi closed too far (open slightly).

catalog_mismatches.manual: ANSI Z21.88-2019/CSA 2.33-2019, Vented Gas Fireplace Heaters; CSA 2.17 2017, Gas-Fired Appliances for Use at High Altitudes

review.notes: Catalog checks that match the manual: BTU NG and LP 35,000 max / 18,000 min (p. 8), 4 x 6-5/8 co-axial vent (p. 36), IPI/CPI selectable ignition (p. 56), mobile/manufactured home approval (p. 1), KZK and KPV options (pp. 12, 36), Class A / masonry conversion (p. 42). Not in the manual text, so not compared: efficiency (71.71% NG / 72.99% LP AFUE), height/width/depth (Figure 2.1 on p. 9 is a drawing with no text), weight (215 lb), view area (32-5/8" x 26-7/8"; the manual only lists the replacement glass with gasket, 31 3/8" x 26 1/4", part 701-005T, p. 69), and whether the blower is standard (the manual lists Fan Kit IPI-028 as a part but never says it is included). Catalog features worth a look: the full-front barriers B36-FRSF2 and B36-PSF2 are approved only with a Komfort Zone Kit (pp. 10-11, 32); the manual names the Traditional (NK36-500) and Birch (NK36-B501) log sets without saying which is standard (p. 46); refractory panel names aren't given, only part numbers (p. 46). Shown only as drawings, so not transcribed (the guide names the figure and page): appliance dimensions and gas line access Fig. 2.1 (p. 9), safety barrier groups Figs. 2.2-2.3 (p. 10), typical installation Fig. 3.3 (p. 16), minimum framing Fig. 3.4 (p. 17), wall pass-through framing Fig. 3.6 (p. 19), outdoor installs Figs. 3.7-3.8 (pp. 20-21), mantel projections Figs. 5.2-5.3 (pp. 26-27), non-combustible zone Fig. 5.5 (p. 29), vertical termination clearances Figs. 7.1-7.2 (p. 34), termination locations Fig. 7.3 (p. 35), combination venting chart Fig. 8.6 (p. 41), wiring Figs. 10.1-10.3 (pp. 49-51), remote overview Fig. 11.1 (p. 55), flame photos (p. 67). Page 52 ('11.0 Operating Instructions') is an image with no extractable text; the guide's lighting steps come from 11.2-11.9 (pp. 53-56). Pages 2, 4, 6 and 72 are blank. Manual errata, not treated as conflicts: 11.9.5 'Turn OFF the appliance' (p. 56) repeats the turn-ON wording, so the guide's turn-off uses 11.7.1.2 (p. 54, press ON/OFF to turn the system OFF) and 11.9.5's result line; 8.2 (p. 37) states 1" on top, sides and bottom of horizontal pipe without repeating the 17-5/8" in-chamber top clearance given in Table 3.1, 3.9.2 and Figs. 5.2-5.3 (pp. 15, 18, 26-27), and the guide uses the in-chamber figure; printed cross-reference page numbers are off throughout (e.g. 8.6 'on page 41' is p. 42, 11.9.3 'page 55' is p. 56, troubleshooting cites Fig. 10.1 'on page 52' (p. 49), 9.1 'page 43' (p. 44), 12.2.3 'page 63' (p. 62), 12.2.1 'page 62' (p. 61)), so the guide uses physical pages; 'Metal Fab*' on p. 36 has no matching footnote; the termination table says 'desk' for deck; the warranty text is dated July 2018 inside the Rev. 4 (August 2024) manual. The remote's SEL/CLR feature toggles (pp. 57-59) and manual-operation reset (11.3, p. 53) are referenced, not reproduced step by step.
